Title: LLMs as Assistants in Software Architecture Design
Claim: Large language models can assist architects in design concept selection by enabling rapid identification, comparison, and exploration of design alternatives, thereby facilitating decision‑making.
Evidence: "This article explores how large language models can assist in this decision‑making process." / "The emergence of generative AI and LLMs, trained on extensive design literature, pattern catalogs, and other solutions, has opened new possibilities to address the design concept selection problem, by enabling users to rapidly identify, compare, and explore design alternatives, and also by facilitating choice."
Labels: LLM, Software Architecture, Design Assistance
Conditions: None
Limits: None

Title: Complexity of Design Concept Selection and Barrier for Inexperienced Designers
Claim: Selecting and instantiating design concepts is inherently complex, requiring substantial knowledge and experience, which creates a barrier for inexperienced designers.
Evidence: "Design concept selection is inherently complex: it requires substantial knowledge and experience to identify viable alternatives for a given problem." / "Identifying viable alternatives can be especially challenging for inexperienced designers, creating a barrier to entry for those new to the design process."
Labels: Design Concept Selection, Software Architecture, Inexperience
Conditions: None
Limits: None
